0: FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 4 ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 5 March 1984, after the draft finalized by the Food Hygiene Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural end Food Products Division Council. such as KHOA, WHOA based sweets, are produced in large quantities in India. It has been often observed that proper hygienic conditions are not maintained in production, transport, storage and distribution of these indigenous milk products and there is a considerable scope for improving the hygienic conditions in this res ect. Unless proper hygienic norms are adopted, the consumption o P such indigenous milk products may be a potential health hazard to the consumer.
DAHI, RASGOLLA, CHkIANA

0.2 Indigenous

milk products,

handling, transport, storage and 0 3 As the process of production, distribution of various indigenous milk products differ very widely, codes of hygienic conditions for different milk products are being published in parts, Part 1 covers hygienic conditions for production, transport, storage and distribution of KHOA and KHOA based sweets, Part 2 covers DAHI, Part 3 covers CHHANA and CHHANA based sweetmeats, and Part 5 covers SHRIKHAND.
0.4 KULk'l

is an indigenous ice cream product prepared by condensing milk to half its volume by heating, adding sugar during boiling and various nuts, MALAI and flavour after cooling and finally freezing the mixture in small moulds. 0.5 Traditionally, cow, buffalo or mixed milk either as such or skimmed partially, is concentrated in a large open pan ( KADAHi, cauldron ) over direct flame. After cooling the concentrate for a while, sugar is added, followed by addition of other ingredients. Alternatively, KHOA

a

IS:lO!V4(Part4)-1984 or skim-milk powder is added to boiled and cooled milk and mixed This mixture is filled in moulds, capped prior to addition of additives.
and caps sealed with wheat dough and finally frozen by immersion in

salt-ice mixture in an earthen pitcher by shaking it to and fro. The frozen product is consumed either as such or alongwith added flavours, SHERBET, SEMIYA and a jelly- like substance popularly known as FALUDA. Since the product contains all the essential nutrients of milk in a concentrated form and added starchy materials, it provides an ideal medium for rapid proliferation of most micro-organisms. During its preparation there is no protection against contamination from extraneous matter, such asjdust, ash, flies and pests. It may, hence, become a potential health hazard and a source of food poisoning. It is, therefore, necessary tq take utmost precautions to protect the commodity from all possible &utce of contamination during proThis standard provides guidlines duction, storage and distribution. for maintaining optimum hygienic conditions in production, storage and distribution of KULFI. 0.6 It is expected that this standard would be of considerable assistance to local health authorities in enforcing proper hygienic conditions in the interest of public health. 0.7 This code is subject to the provisioils of the Prevent@ of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the rules fi-amed thereunder as ammended from time to time and other local regulation. 0.8 While preparing this standard, considerable assistance derived from the National Dairy Research Institute, Karnal.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This code ( Part 4 ) prescribes the hygienic conditions and practices for production, storage, transportation and distribution of KULFI and the like milk products. 2. SITE AND PREMISES 2.1 Site and 19s4*. premises should be as given in 2 of IS : 10974 ( Part 1 ) HANDLING

IS : 10974 ( Part 4 ) - 1984 4. FACTdRY AND PROCESSING 4.1 Factory and processing IS : 2491-1972*. 5. EQUIPMENTS 5.1 Heating Pans 5.1.1
KADAHIES KULFZ.

HYGIENE should be as given in 5 of

hygiene

shall be constructed with hzmisphericsl or dished bottom and should have rigid we!ded handles. The joints in the pan shall be welded and finished smooth. The component p'arts shall not be riveted. The KADAHI may be of 20 to 25 litres capacity. 5.2 Heating of Milk

5.2.1 Ovens of different types are used for heating of milk in the small scale production of KULFI. Wood, charcoal, coal, cow dung cake, kerosene or gas, are normally used as fuel. 5.2.2 When open hearth is used, the fuel used for burning shoud not give rise to smoke or obnoxious odour which may be absorbed by the product. Adequate protection must be provided to ventilate the combustion products and to prevent the ash and unburnt material coming in contact with the product. 5.2.3 Where heating is done by steam in large scale operations, the pan shall conform to IS : 2829-1979t. Stainless steel jacketted, round bottomed open pan provided with steam line, steam control and safety valves, pressure gauge and cold water line in the jackets, with steam trap and air outlet may be used. There should be arrangement for tilting the pan and also keeping it fixed in normal position. 5.3 Stirrers - During heating of milk, the contents in the heating pan are constantly stirred to facilitate evaporation of moisture and to prevent charring of casein. For thrs purpose, steel, hand operated stirrers are generally used. Stainless steel or aluminium alloy stirrers with flattened end on one side may preferably be used in place of iron. Suitable arrangement may be made on the brim of the heating pan for resting of stirrers. 5.4 All the components and metallic parts which come in contact with milk shall be constructed from iron or stainless steel conforming *Code for hygienic conditions for food processing units (first revision ). $Specification for steam-jacketed GHEE pans ( stainless steel ) (first revision ).

5.6 Non metallic materials, if used for sealing or gasketting shall be nontoxic, non absorbent and shall not impart any flavour and should be inert to milk, KULFZ or any cleaning solution normally used. 5.7 Fabrication - All surfaces coming in contact with milk or KULFI shall be finished smooth, free from pits, crevices or other constructional features which might inhibit satisfactory sanitation, 5.8 Containers ( Moulds, Cones ) 5.8.1 Usually galvanized iron sheet moulds are used. They have a conical shape and diameter of about 2'5 cm at the bottom and 5.0 cfzl at the top with a length of about 7'5 cm and nicely fitting lids. This size may vary with the requirements of the manufacturer. 5.8.1.1 Plastic containers of above size also are now m vogue-which are comparatively more hygienical. 5.8.2 Cleaning and sterilization 5.9 Freezing Equipment 5.9.1 An earthen pot ( pitcher) of about 30 to 40 litre capacity which It shall can freeze about 50 to 60 moulds at a time is generally used. be thoroughly cleaned, washed and sanitized, before and after every use everyday using a good brush ( preferably of synthetic bristles ), and an odourless bactericidal solution, such as quaternary ammonium compounds. 5.9.2 Salt-Ice Mixture - A good quantity of a chipped ice with about 20 percent of common salt, or some times rock salt, is added into the pitcher. The salt and ice shall be of good grade free from visible Ice used shall be manu+ impurities, dust, and hygienically collected. factured from potable water. 5.9.3 Wheat flour used fur preparing the dough for sealing the lids of' moulds with the main body shall be made from a good quality wheat

RECEPTION DOCK 6.1 Milk brought to the factory shall be received in an airy spacious enclosure. Only fresh, sweet, clean milk free from colostrum and in every way fit for human consumption shall be used. The milk shall be free from adulterants, preservatives and any matter foreign to milk. 7. mixture shall be allowed to cool for a while at the room before filling into cones ( moulds ).

Filling in Cones - The KULFI mixture shall be filled up to the in the cones, covered tightly with the lid and sealed with a thick of dough ( see 5.9.3 ). Rubber bands may also be used for fastethe lids before applying dough.

10.3 Freezing the Filled Cones - The cones shafl be transferred to the ice-salt mixture in the pitcher without losing time. The pitcher shall be shaken to and fro thoroughly to bring about effective freezing in a short time.

OF KtJLFY

11.1 The finished product shall be allowed to remain ia the same pitcher or, transferred to, deep freeze at - 20�C for storage at the manufacturer's premises,
12. TRANSPORT 12.1 The KULFZ should be trarrsporfed bgr suitable system, ip1 the pitcher or in an ice-chest containing ice-salt mixture. The transport vehicle shall be clean and made such as not to give any jerks during movement. *Specification for cheese knife.

IS : 10974 ( Part 4 ) - 1984 13. STORAGE AND SALE

OF KULFZ

13.1 The finished product shall always be stored in the cones kept in ice-salt mixture which should be .r*plenished from time to time. It shall not be carried over to the next day.

13.2 The push cart used for storing and selling KULFZ shall have a metallic roof and the walls made of good grade glass panes. It shall be provided with a sliding window for removing KULFZ from the ice chest. Utmost care shall be taken to protect the inside of the push carts from roadside dust, flies, other insects, birds and rodents. 13.3 The knife (see IS : 249%1963* ) used to scrape away the dough from the cone and open its cap and subsequently cut the KULFZ into pieces shall be made from good qual'ity mild steel or stainless steel and kept clean and dry. It shall be sanitized in quaternary ammonium compounds or iodophor solution. 13.4 The plates and spoons used for serving the preparation shhll be thoroughly cleaned and rinsed before use and given a dip or two in a sanitizer solution, for example, quarternary ammonium compound ( 50 ppm ), iodophor ( 5 ppm ), or chlorine solution ( 15-20 ppm ) just prior to adding KULFZ on to the plate. 13.4.1 The used utensi!s shall be washed in fresh water, preferably running tap water, using soap or detergent solution and then drained and dried. 13.5 Suitable arrangements shall be made for proper drainage disposal of wash and waste water ( see 3.12 of IS : 2491-1972t ). 14.
